page: Microsoft Azure D8s_v3 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DSv3 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 4 physical Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz and includes a 50 MB L3 cache. This instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, translating to 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It also includes a 66 GB local SSD and supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark results indicate that the D8s_v3 delivers modest compute and memory performance. Single-core metrics, such as the stress-ng single-core CPU test and Geekbench single-core score, fall into the weak and poor categories respectively, reflecting its older Broadwell-generation architecture. Multi-core performance is relatively stronger, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and PassMark memory scores reaching average levels. However, memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks consistently rank in the bottom 25%, and data decompression tasks show poor performance.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D8s_v3 offers a balanced resource density of vCPUs to memory, making it a viable option for legacy workloads that do not require high single-threaded performance. It is suited for general-purpose applications, moderate database operations, basic web serving, and lightweight development environments. However, for compute-intensive tasks, high-throughput databases, or modern LLM inference, newer instance generations with updated CPU architectures will provide better resource-to-performance ratios.
description: Microsoft Azure D8s_v3 is a general-purpose virtual machine from the DSv3 family, powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor. It provides 8 dedicated vCPUs (4 physical cores with hyper-threading) running at 2.3 GHz, 32.0 GB of RAM, and a 66 GB local SSD with Premium Storage support. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, its performance profile is characterized by average multi-core CPU and memory scores, though single-core compute and memory bandwidth benchmarks generally fall into the lower percentiles. This resource balance makes the D8s_v3 qualitatively cost-effective for steady-state, non-burstable workloads that require a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It is best suited for general-purpose applications, moderate web serving, and development environments rather than high-performance computing or intensive database operations.
